title: Hornbills of the Pakke Tiger Reserve
body: The Pakke Tiger Reserve in Arunachal Pradesh is a forest where scientists have recorded nearly 300 bird species, a striking number given that India as a whole has about 1,300 bird species. Pakke supports four species of hornbills: the Rufous-necked Hornbill, the Oriental Pied Hornbill, the Great Hornbill and the Wreathed Hornbill. These large birds nest only in large, old trees that have suitable cavities, and they feed on specific fruits. As a result, different hornbill species are found in different parts of the forest, depending on tree size and fruit availability. Studying and classifying such patterns helps scientists ask precise questions about how species are distributed and which plants and animals are closely linked.
